change_interpretations.engineering_summary: The maximum allowed time for the torque controller to issue demanded positive torque after validated pedal input above 70% is reduced from 100 ms to 80 ms. This is a tightening of the performance requirement, which may invalidate previous PASS evidence that measured response times between 80 ms and 100 ms. Test procedures and scripts that reference the old 100 ms limit must be updated, and affected tests must be rerun to generate new evidence.

assessments.reason: The test directly verifies the driver torque response time. The previous evidence of 94 ms no longer meets the tightened 80 ms requirement, and the test procedure still references the old 100 ms threshold.
evidence: TV-001 procedure explicitly checks for torque response within 100 ms
Previous result was PASS at 94 ms
New requirement VCU-DR-01 tightens the limit to 80 ms
94 ms exceeds the new 80 ms limit
assessments.recommended_action: Update the test procedure and script to use the 80 ms threshold, then rerun the test to generate new evidence.

assessments.reason: The test exercises the changed requirement but does not explicitly measure or report the torque response time in its procedure or previous result. It is unclear if the previous PASS evidence covers the new timing constraint.
evidence: TV-002 is linked to VCU-DR-01
Procedure involves 85% pedal demand
Comment states 'Timing not reported in old evidence'
New requirement tightens torque response time to 80 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Review the test procedure to determine if timing is measured; if not, update the procedure to include timing measurement and rerun.

assessments.reason: The test content (torque response time measurement) is clearly related to the changed requirement, but the link is missing. The previous result of 92 ms exceeds the new 80 ms limit, and the legacy tolerance of 95 ms is also invalid.
evidence: TV-003 has a missing requirement link
Procedure sweeps demand 75-95% and recorded 92 ms
Comment states 'Legacy suite still checks 95 ms tolerance'
New requirement VCU-DR-01 tightens limit to 80 ms
assessments.recommended_action: Clarify the requirement link with the system engineer, update the tolerance to 80 ms, and rerun the test.

assessments.reason: The test verifies brake actuator response, which is governed by the unchanged VCU-BRK-03. The workshop notes explicitly warn against conflating brake latency with positive torque response time, so the change to VCU-DR-01 does not affect this test.
evidence: TV-004 is linked to VCU-BRK-03 (unchanged)
Workshop notes state brake command latency and positive torque command latency use different clocks
Procedure targets brake command latency, not positive torque response
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this change.

No relation to driver torque response time
assessments.recommended_action: No action required for this change.

assessments.reason: The test content (torque delivery at high pedal demand) plausibly relates to the changed requirement, but the link is TBD and ownership is unclear. The test has not been run, so there is no evidence to assess against the new limit.

assessments.recommended_action: Clarify the requirement link and ownership, then determine if the test needs to be run against the new 80 ms limit.
